title: Pixels2Actions
hook: Practiced only inside a *computer*. Can it work for real?

segments.label: PAPER
segments.headline: Practice in a computer, work for real

beats.narration: Robots usually learn a new skill from recordings of real robots doing it. So can a robot that practiced only inside a computer work in the real world?
Researchers let a small AI practice moving robot arms only inside a computer.
Then they tested it on a real robot, on tasks it had never practiced.
It succeeded twenty-nine times out of thirty, as well as a much bigger AI tested the same way.
The researchers' point: a new skill means new practice in the computer, not new robot recordings.
